ruleName: Marking and picking up the ball
title: How to mark your ball on the green
question: Which of these can you use to mark your ball’s position on the green? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Your putter placed behind the ball

explanation: You are allowed to use a coin, a ball-marker, or a tee to mark your ball on the putting green. Placing your putter down does not count as a proper marker.

juniorVersion.title: What can you use to show where your ball is on the green?
juniorVersion.question: Pick all the things you are allowed to use to show your ball's spot on the green before you pick it up.
juniorVersion.explanation: You can use a coin, a round ball-marker, or a tee to show where your ball is before you pick it up on the green. You can't just put your putter behind the ball to mark it—that does not count.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth, short grass area where you try to putt the ball into the hole.
A small, flat object you put behind your ball to remember its place.
A small stick you use to hold the ball up, but you can also use it to mark where your ball is on the green.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how to mark their ball by using a coin, marker, or tee, and explain why a club is not okay.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think it's okay to just use their putter as a marker.
Some might wonder if they can use anything, not just the items listed.
